bw: Progressive quadriparesis, neck pain on coughing
w: A cerebellar astrocytoma causes ataxia and hydrocephalus, not progressive quadriparesis from cord compression.
Multiple sclerosis is relapsing-remitting with multifocal lesions and rarely causes cough-induced neck pain.
p: Foramen magnum tumors compress the cervicomedullary junction, causing spastic quadriparesis, lower cranial nerve signs and neck pain worse with Valsalva.

bw: Recurrent infections, oral thrush since birth
w: B cell deficiency causes recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections after maternal IgG wanes, not fungal and viral infections from birth.
Selective IgA deficiency is mostly asymptomatic or causes mild mucosal infections.
p: Severe combined immunodeficiency: absent T cell function with recurrent opportunistic infections, thrush and failure to thrive; treat with stem cell transplant.

bw: Demands to speak to 'whoever is in charge'
w: Histrionic patients seek attention with dramatic emotion rather than status and entitlement.
Borderline patients show unstable relationships, identity and mood, with idealization and devaluation.
p: Narcissistic personality disorder: grandiosity, need for admiration, entitlement and lack of empathy; self-esteem is fragile.

w: Statins are not associated with Clostridioides difficile infection.
Calcium and vitamin D supplements do not alter C. difficile risk.
p: C. difficile risk factors: recent antibiotics, hospitalization, advanced age and proton pump inhibitors; treat with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin.

x: ST depression also consistent with unstable angina

w: FSH and LH show hypergonadotropic hypogonadism but do not identify the chromosomal cause.
17-hydroxyprogesterone screens for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which virilizes.
p: Delayed puberty with high FSH/LH suggests ovarian failure; karyotype detects Turner syndrome (45,X) or other chromosomal causes.

bw: Older woman, temporal headache, pain when chewing
w: Oxygen is for cluster headache, which does not threaten vision.
Simple analgesics do not prevent blindness from giant cell arteritis.
p: Suspected giant cell arteritis needs immediate high-dose glucocorticoids to prevent blindness, before temporal artery biopsy.

bw: Found down at construction site, drenched in sweat
w: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome features lead-pipe rigidity and absent sweating over days.
Malignant hyperthermia occurs with volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine.
p: Exertional heat stroke: core temperature above 40 C with altered mentation after heat exposure; treat with rapid cooling.

w: D2 blockers relieve nausea but are adjunctive rather than the next abortive choice here.
Beta-blockers are prophylactic, not abortive.
p: Triptans abort migraine through serotonin receptor agonism; they are contraindicated in coronary disease and hemiplegic migraine.

w: Topical antibiotics do not treat systemic Bordetella infection.
Tobramycin drops treat bacterial conjunctivitis, not pertussis.
p: Pertussis is treated with a macrolide (azithromycin) mainly to reduce transmission; treat contacts and ensure vaccination.

bw: Sudden severe leg pain, pale cold limb
w: Leriche syndrome is chronic aortoiliac occlusion with claudication and impotence.
Buerger disease affects young smokers with segmental thrombosis of small vessels.
p: Acute limb ischemia (the 6 Ps: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia) from embolus in AF needs urgent heparin and revascularization.

w: Shoulder radiographs would not evaluate the likely splenic injury causing referred pain.
Shoulder MRI is not an emergency test and misses abdominal trauma.
p: Splenic injury refers pain to the left shoulder (Kehr sign); stable patients get abdominal CT, unstable patients go to laparotomy.

w: Metronidazole treats bacterial vaginosis or trichomonas, which are absent (normal pH).
Metformin treats gestational diabetes and does not prevent preterm birth.
p: A short cervix (under 25 mm) before 24 weeks is treated with vaginal progesterone; cerclage is for prior preterm birth or very short cervix with history.
